title: Network buffer buildup & CNI qdisc latency post-incident notes
content:
Summary:

On 2026-03-09 (09:40 UTC) our east-us cluster experienced a progressive increase in P95/P99 request latency for inference endpoints followed by a surge in pod start latency and several control-plane reconcilers reporting timeouts. Surface impact: ~12% of requests experienced >300ms additional tail latency for a 35m window; concurrent rolling updates failed to reach desired replicas for ~20% of deployments in the cluster. No customer data was lost; primarily latency and pod readiness breakage.

Why this document exists / intent:
- Capture timeline and evidence for a network buffer/qdisc-related kernel transmit backlog that cascaded into CNI dataplane pressure, conntrack exhaustion, kube-proxy instability, and delayed scheduler bindings.
- Draft a short emergency runbook to mitigate similar incidents and a set of long-term fixes.
- Surface open questions to follow up with infra/serving-runtime teams.

High-level hypothesis (short):
A combination of (1) increased egress burst from a set of model-serving pods, (2) changes to host-level qdisc settings from a recent kernel tuning PR, and (3) an under-provisioned conntrack table caused transmit queue buildup on host NICs -> packets queued in kernel -> tx drops/retransmits -> higher network tail latency -> kube-proxy/conntrack churn and kubelet pod start stalls. Additionally, disk IO contention on masters slowed etcd compaction which amplified control-plane timeouts.

Timeline (collected notes):
- 09:35 UTC: Spike in egress bytes and TCP retransmits on nodes in nodepool-gpu-12 (alerts: net.tcp.retransmits > baseline).
- 09:38 UTC: P95 latency for API gateway starts climbing, tracing shows increased downstream waits on worker calls.
- 09:40 UTC: Autoscaler/rolling-update jobs observe many pods in ContainerCreating/NetworkUnavailable for >60s.
- 09:45 UTC: conntrack in kube-proxy logs: "conntrack: table full, dropping entries" on 4 nodes.
- 09:50 UTC: kube-scheduler reports "failed to bind pod" with rpc timeouts to kube-apiserver. Some master nodes report high I/O wait.
- 10:05 UTC: first mitigation applied (manual sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max ++ on affected nodes); partial recovery of pod readiness after ~5–8 minutes.
- 10:20 UTC: applied temporary qdisc change on two host NICs (set fq_codel / increase txqueuelen) -> notable drop in retransmits and latency returns toward baseline by ~10:45–11:00 UTC.

Detection signals / what alerted us:
- net.tcp.retransmits alert (node-exporter + custom eBPF counters)
- conntrack table fill logs from kube-proxy
- pod start latency (monitoring synthetic job) and many ContainerCreating states in the deployment dashboard
- API server request latencies and etcd op latency (metric etcd_server_proposals_committed_monitor_total latency)

Evidence collected:
- sar/iostat on control-plane showed increased svctm and %iowait between 09:42–10:10 UTC correlated with etcd leader churn events in logs.
- tcpdump on affected nodes showed long queuing delays and repeated retransmit (tstamp deltas > 200ms before ack).
- tc -s qdisc showed large backlog for pfifo_fast on eno1: qlen near txqueuelen limits; after fq_codel change queue depth reduced.
- ss -s and conntrack -L showed large number of TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED sockets for specific service IP ranges.
- dmesg: a few "nf_conntrack: table full" kernel warnings on startup of high-traffic pods.

Immediate mitigations executed (chronological):
1) Raised nf_conntrack_max from 262144 to 524288 on affected nodes (short term) and flushed conntrack entries to free space (conntrack -F) where safe.
2) Toggled host qdisc to fq_codel for NICs on two worst hosts and increased txqueuelen from 1000 to 20000 (targets: low-latency queues for bursts).
3) Scaled kube-proxy pods to multiple replicas and rolled to a build with better conntrack handling (stopgap: increase conntrack hashsize).
4) Deprioritized large reconfiguration jobs (paused rollout job queue) to let control plane catch up.
5) Throttled egress on the offending workload as a temporary rate limit (iptables tc policing) to reduce burstiness.

Effect of mitigations:
- conntrack warnings subsided ~6–8 minutes after the sysctl bump and flush.
- After fq_codel + txqueuelen change, TCP retransmits dropped by ~70% and P95 latency returned close to baseline over ~20 minutes.
- Pod start latency improved but did not immediate fully normalize until control-plane IO pressure reduced (etcd compaction completed).

Root cause analysis (detailed reasoning):
- Primary: Host-side transmit queue exhaustion. The netlink qdisc in use (pfifo_fast) with the previously deployed txqueuelen and a kernel qdisc tuning PR committed last month made the host unable to absorb short high-throughput bursts; packets were queued and incurred large queueing latency and drops.
- Secondary: conntrack table size was tuned down earlier to conserve memory for GPU nodes; this left insufficient headroom for a high-concurrency burst pattern, which produced "table full" events that caused packet drops and kube-proxy churn.
- Tertiary: control-plane IO (etcd) became a visible amplification factor. When many pods are delayed, the control plane sees a burst of reconciliations; etcd compaction ran into IO contention (noisy neighbor on masters due to backup job scheduled same window) and leadership elections increased API latency, compounding pod start delays.

Why we didn't detect earlier / detection gaps:
- No alert specifically correlating tx queue length with application-level latency. We monitor retransmits, but no runbook tied retransmit spikes to qdisc mismatches.
- Conntrack headroom tuning change was documented in a PR but not linked to the runtime risk register for nodepool-gpu-12 (ownership gap).
- Backups/maintenance jobs on masters were scheduled during a high-traffic window — lack of cross-team coordination.

Short-term follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Avery Chen (owner): roll a cluster-wide emergency change to restore nf_conntrack_max to conservative default for GPUs; add temporary guardrails to PCF to prevent over-aggressive conntrack reductions. (due: 2026-03-13)
- Marcus Patel: create an alert that triggers when tc qlen approaches 75% txqueuelen on any host and tie to paging the oncall (due: 2026-03-14).
- Leah O'Neill: adjust master maintenance window policy and coordinate backup schedule (due: 2026-03-16).
- Diego Ramirez: shepherd kube-proxy change PR that increases hashsize and adds defensive logging when conntrack table pressure occurs (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-ops/pull/118) (due: 2026-03-18).

Long-term remediation proposals (discussion items):
- Default to fq_codel on all NICs for nodepools that host high-burst workloads and tune txqueuelen based on NIC type and driver; build a validation test for new kernel/qdisc tuning PRs in ci that simulates bursty egress.
- Revisit conntrack tuning policy: move to per-node profiling (based on workload class) and add automatic scaling of nf_conntrack_max for burst events with throttling rather than global static reduction.
- Move kube-proxy to IPVS mode cluster-wide (reduces conntrack pressure for certain patterns) and validate behavior at scale.
- Add egress shaping primitives at CNI level (calico/eps) so a single noisy pod cannot flood host transmit queues.
- Prevent backups/noisy IO jobs from running on masters during known high-traffic windows; move compaction throttles to reduce impact.

Draft emergency runbook (quick-action checklist) — for oncall SREs:
1) Alert triage: Confirm retransmit and conntrack alerts; identify top-3 affected nodes via net.tcp.retransmits and conntrack logs.
2) If conntrack table full: temporarily increase nf_conntrack_max by 2x on affected nodes: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
3) If nf_conntrack is already > 512k and still full, run safe flush: sudo conntrack -D --orig-port-src  (warning: be conservative; check sessions)
4) Inspect host qdisc: sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eno1; if pfifo_fast has backlog ~= txqueuelen, switch to fq_codel: sudo tc qdisc replace dev eno1 root fq_codel
5) Increase txqueuelen for test nodes: sudo ip link set dev eno1 txqueuelen 20000
6) Pause large cluster-wide rollouts (coordinate with release owner)
7) Apply temporary egress rate limit for noisy workload: tc qdisc add dev eno1 root handle 1: htb default 30; tc class add ... (team-specific snippet kept in private playbook)
8) Monitor: conntrack -S, ss -s, kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n <ns>, etcd metrics, API server latency.
9) If control-plane IO high: check backups and postpone; move heavy IO jobs off masters.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did the recent kernel/qdisc tuning PR land without a CI test that simulates short-burst 10s-100s Mbps flows? (action: infra-ci team)
- Are there workload patterns we can proactively label as "burst-prone" and place on nodes with tuned qdisc by default? (action: serving-runtime)
- Is conntrack tuning consistent across cloud regions and nodepod types? Need audit of all nodepool-specific sysctls.

Action items (concrete tickets to create):
- SRE-3421: Implement tc/qdisc smoke test in infra CI and block merging of kernel/qdisc tuning PRs until test passes (owner Marcus)
- SRE-3422: Conntrack audit across nodepools + create auto-scaling controller for nf_conntrack_max (owner Avery)
- SRE-3423: IPVS feasibility spike for kube-proxy migration (owner Diego)

Notes to self / scribbles: 
- We were lucky that txqueuelen increase + fq_codel diff fixed things w/o heavy infra churn; this is brittle.
- Need to add a short doc on how to safely flush conntrack on production without disrupting stateful workloads.
- Consider embedding a small eBPF probe that measures tx queue latency and exposes it as a prometheus metric (would have caught this earlier).

Appendix: useful commands observed during triage
- tc -s qdisc show dev eno1
- sudo ip link set dev eno1 txqueuelen 20000
- sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
- sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
- sudo conntrack -F   # use cautiously; can drop active sessions
- ss -s
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>  # look for NetworkUnavailable / CNI errors
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 100

If anything is unclear or you have extra traces/pcaps, paste them into SRE-3421 thread. I'll update this doc after the three follow-ups land and when we have the CI test PR ready.

-- Avery

(rough, intentionally chatty; will convert to a polished postmortem once root-cause tickets are prioritized)
